protocol_notes: Gold category/severity/form for the published catalog are in codebook/incidents.json (Table III).
The round is not blinded against that catalog.
The coder worked from codebook/second-coder/PACKET.md only and did not browse the repository before submit.
Agreement is label assignment given Table I, not taxonomy discovery and not a multi-estate reliability claim.
primary_metric_rationale: Severity is skewed (Table III 1/9/1). Cohen's kappa understates agreement under that prevalence (kappa paradox). Gwet AC1 is the intended primary chance-corrected metric; kappa is reported alongside.

computation.cohen_kappa: standard (Po-Pe)/(1-Pe) with Pe from rater marginal products
computation.gwet_ac1: Gwet AC1: (Po-Pe)/(1-Pe) with Pe=(1/(q-1))*sum_k pi_k*(1-pi_k); pi_k=mean of two raters' category proportions; q=scheme size (10 categories / 3 severities)
references: Gwet, K. L. (2008). Computing inter-rater reliability and its variance in the presence of high agreement. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 61(1), 29-48.

severity.ci_note: kappa CI spans [0,1] under Sev-2 dominance; AC1 remains the primary chance-corrected read

disagreements.note: Coder read conflicting replica state as trustworthiness/security-boundary risk (Sev-3); author catalog is Sev-2 (cohort/site ops intervention).
disagreements.rubric_boundary: Informative Sev-2/Sev-3 judgment at the seam where stale or conflicting auth state shades into wrong-trust risk. Evidence the severity rubric has real content there, not that category coding failed.

not_included: Case-to-incident shuffle map (author-only; keeps future packet sheets from becoming a lookup table)
